title: Glia Cell Morphology Analysis Using the Fiji GliaMorph Toolkit
author: Kugler, Breitenbach, et al.

steps.title: Assess 3D data quality
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the 3‑D image stack in Fiji 3D Viewer, examine voxel properties across neighboring slices, and quantitatively evaluate signal‑to‑noise (SNR) or contrast‑to‑noise (CNR) ratios to identify any depth‑related quality issues.

steps.title: Process AiryScan images
steps.instruction: Apply AiryScan processing using the non‑iterative linear Wiener deconvolution algorithm as described in the microscope manual (Huff 2015; Zeiss 2019).

steps.title: Convert and prepare AiryScan files
steps.instruction: Convert raw files (e.g., .czi) to .tiff with Bio‑Formats, crop and orient the images for comparability, split multi‑channel files, and optionally perform a 1‑D vector analysis.

substeps.instruction: Crop and orient images to improve comparability.
Split multi‑channel images into separate files.

steps.title: Prepare confocal images and PSF
steps.instruction: For confocal data, set up PSF deconvolution: specify channel count and fluorophore emission wavelengths, provide objective NA, indicate whether an experimental PSF exists, and either load the PSF file or generate a theoretical PSF with the Diffraction PSF 3D plugin.

substeps.instruction: Enter fluorophore emission wavelengths (e.g., 510 nm for GFP in channel 1, 586 nm for dsRed in channel 2).
Provide objective numerical aperture (NA) if a theoretical PSF is needed.
Indicate if an experimental PSF file exists; if not, generate a theoretical PSF using the Diffraction PSF 3D plugin.
Load the selected or generated PSF into DeconvolutionLab2.

steps.title: Select input folder and crop
steps.instruction: Choose the folder containing the .tiff files acquired in confocal mode and, if desired, run the SubregionTool to crop the data before deconvolution to reduce computational load.

substeps.instruction: Select the folder with the .tiff files.
Optionally apply SubregionTool to create a smaller sub‑region for faster deconvolution.

steps.title: Run deconvolution (Richardson‑Lucy, 1 iteration)
steps.instruction: Execute Richardson‑Lucy deconvolution in DeconvolutionLab2 on each channel using the selected or generated PSF, setting the iteration count to 1.

substeps.instruction: Run deconvolution for each channel with the appropriate PSF.

steps.title: Choose and apply segmentation method
steps.instruction: Review available 3‑D segmentation approaches, select the method best suited to the image properties (e.g., thresholding, watershed, machine‑learning), and apply it to the deconvolved stacks.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate segmentation options based on image characteristics.
Apply the chosen segmentation to the deconvolved data.

steps.title: Post‑process segmentation (remove speckles)
steps.instruction: After segmentation, filter out small speckles (e.g., using a size‑threshold filter) to improve segmentation quality.

substeps.instruction: Apply a size‑filter to remove objects below a defined voxel count.

steps.title: Run GliaMorph quantitative analysis
steps.instruction: Load the processed segmentation into the GliaMorph toolkit and run the quantification tool for large‑scale analysis of glial cell morphology.
